Alex — thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation I put together a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused specifically on performance benchmarking and regional routing behavior so we can land on SLA/backstop numbers for the pilot. High-level asks: 

- Redwood will run a controlled benchmark against your representative inference workload (3 prompts, ~512 context on average) across US/EU/APAC regions. Metrics: throughput (requests/sec), concurrency (clients), p50/p95/p99 latency for TTFT and per-token, and end-to-end TTFT at 1, 5, 10, 25 concurrent users.
- We'll exercise multi-region routing and failover: traffic switchover time, error rates during failover, and cold-cache impact.
- Deliverables: report with raw CSV, summary slides, and runbook for your SREs.

Proposed timeline:
- This week (Mar 2–5): Redwood runs baseline runs and a multi-region failover test.
- Mar 8: joint results review + map update.
- Mar 12: signoff for pilot roll (if results meet thresholds).

Can you confirm the three representative prompts (I attached 3 sample prompts in the MAP PDF) and permission to run load from our hosted runners in us-west, eu-west, and ap-northeast regions? Also looping in Rishi and Stephanie to own test setup and results.

Thanks,

Subject: Benchmark plan (test harness + measurement details)

Alex / team — quick note on how we'll run these so results are actionable. Test harness: k6 driver with custom client that exercises streaming, measuring: time-to-first-token (TTFT) from request start, server-side token emit times, per-token latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV lookup hit rates (for caching effect).

Matrix we'll run (each run repeated 3x; median reported):
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 5, 10, 25, 100 concurrent clients (10s ramps, 2 min stable window)
- Sequence lengths: mean 128, 256, 512 (your sample set is ~512 average)
- Regions: us-west, eu-west, ap-northeast (runners pinned to region)
- Failover scenarios: graceful region drain (route traffic away), sudden region outage (kill runner), and cold-cache injection (clearing Redis/KV between runs).

Pass criteria proposed (we can adjust after review):
- TTFT p95 <= 300 ms (warm); p95 <= 800 ms (cold)
- Throughput per instance >= 40 tokens/sec sustained for 512 context at p50 CPU/GPU utilization < 70%
- Failover: 95% of requests successfully rerouted within 3s and service error rate < 1% during event window.

I'll own the harness and will push scripts to the shared Drive link. Any tweaks, call them out before EOD Wed.

—Stephanie
Staff SWE, Redwood Inference

Quick ops note on sampling and measurement windows — we'll capture both client-observed and server-observed timestamps and correlate by request-id so we can split network vs. inference time. For multi-region routing tests we'll run two variants:

1) Region-local: caller -> region-runner -> local model instance (baseline).
2) Cross-region routing: caller -> us-runner -> eu-model (simulate misrouting) to measure penalty; this helps tune routing policy thresholds.

We'll tag runs with run-id and keep raw CSVs attached to the MAP. Expect initial raw export by Thu morning (Mar 5).

—Rishi

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@clariotech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Li Wei <cloudops@clariotech.com>, Dana Collins <procurement@clariotech.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark results export + summary (run-id: CL-2026-031-R1)

Alex — attaching the initial results and a short summary. Raw CSV attached (perf_results_20260305.csv). Highlights (median of 3 runs unless noted):

Summary — regional TTFT and throughput (512 context, streaming enabled):
- US (us-west runner to us-hosted model): concurrency=10 -> TTFT p50=85 ms, p95=220 ms, p99=410 ms; throughput per instance = 48 tokens/sec; sustained error rate 0.1%.
- EU (eu-west): concurrency=10 -> TTFT p50=110 ms, p95=260 ms, p99=520 ms; throughput = 45 tokens/sec; error rate 0.2%.
- APAC (ap-northeast): concurrency=10 -> TTFT p50=140 ms, p95=340 ms, p99=720 ms; throughput = 40 tokens/sec; error rate 0.4%.

Cold vs warm cache (US, concurrency=5): cold TTFT p95=710 ms; warm TTFT p95=210 ms — shows KV cache reduces TTFT substantially.

Failover measurements (sudden outage simulated at t=60s in a 3-min run):
- Scenario: eu-west runner killed, traffic reweighted to us-west and ap-northeast. Observed detection + reroute median = 2.8 s; 95th = 4.6 s.
- Client-visible error spike: brief increase in 502/504s, peak error rate 2.6% for a 6s window, then back to <0.5%.
- Cold-cache penalty during failover (traffic moving to a region with empty KV) added +430 ms p95 on TTFT until cache warmed (~45s).

Cross-region routing penalty (caller us-west -> eu-model): added median latency of +120 ms vs region-local.

Attachments: full CSV, run metadata, and a short slide with graphs. Early interpretation: we meet p95 <= 300 ms warm in US and EU; APAC is close to threshold and could improve with a regional quantized model instance or edge caching. Failover detection and reroute times meet our 3s median expectation but tail exposure (p95/p99) and the cold-cache penalty need a mitigations plan (proactive cache pre-warm on failover, shorter cache TTLs for critical routes).

Next steps proposed:
- Redwood will run a targeted APAC-focused run with a quantization profile (TBD) to see throughput gains.
- We'll draft a short runbook for pre-warm on failover and share by Mon Mar 8.
- Joint review scheduled Mar 8 at 10:00 PT.

—Vivek
Head of Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
